design_finding_recorded_this_round: The done-condition whitelist (URL HOST / marker text / element presence / count) CANNOT express 'a different page on the SAME host'. Example (test 5): 'the DINNER category page is showing' on allrecipes.com has NO expressible condition that distinguishes the homepage from the category page — urlHost matches both; markerText 'Dinner' matches the homepage's own nav link. This is the deep cause of D1 (writers reach for weak proxies because the vocabulary lacks URL identity beyond the host) and part of D3. The ratified §4 text ('the outcome's URL/title identity') covers the fix: 10C.1 adds a URL-IDENTITY condition shape (a URL path/segment predicate, e.g. UrlContains) to the whitelist + schema + checker + render + writer prompt + Tier A fixtures (retire-and-add).
validator_design_decisions_for_10C1_next: Shared evaluation: the validator calls the EXISTING DoneConditionChecker.satisfied(condition, evidence) — one source of truth, no duplicate guard logic.
Validation points: ladder build (after the writer returns) AND every subtask entry (pointer advance + after every re-plan), against the current observation's evidence.

Already-true policy: a URL-identity condition (UrlHost/UrlContains) already true at entry is LEGITIMATE — the code-triggered check verifies and advances immediately (the observed subtask-1-on-the-right-site behaviour must not regress). A WEAK-shaped condition (markerText/elementPresent/count) already true at entry is proxy-suspect: ONE bounded writer repair (bumped prompt version, metered into WriterBudget) → else a code-derived URL/title identity where derivable → else refuse the ladder through the existing loud LADDER_REFUSED path.
Never a silent self-satisfying ladder; ART-4/ART-5 intact.
